title: SMC again supports no super changes
full_text:
The Super Members Council (SMC) has welcomed the call from Liberal MP Garth Hamilton that no government should mess with superannuation.
“I think we should be offering no changes at all to how it’s invested, taxed or accessed,” Hamilton said during a recent television interview.
“I think the economy is so tight at the moment the idea of a comfortable and relaxed retirement for people is slipping away and as the party that has always prided itself on being strong economic managers, I think we should be taking that confidence and security in people’s super forward as a policy position.”
The SMC indicated the opposition assistant energy security and affordability spokesman’s comments reflected Australians’ clear views on super and the recognition its purpose is to provide greater financial safety, security and dignity in retirement.
“[His] comments reflect what Australians instinctively understand: super will be your pay cheque in retirement and it shouldn’t be undermined or diverted to other policy problems,” SMC chief executive Misha Schubert noted.
“Withdrawing super early would just hurt battling Australians by further stoking inflation and interest rates and making it even harder for struggling households to make ends meet.”
To support its position, the SMC pointed to research that found 89 per cent of seniors believe superannuation should be saved for retirement and that they are concerned about early release proposals.
Hamilton’s position contrasts previous coalition proposed policy where opposition treasury spokesman Tim Wilson supported the idea taken to the last election of allowing first-home buyers to access some of their super for a residence.
When asked if the majority of Liberal members of parliament shared his views, Hamilton said: “I think so and we will probably find out over time.
“I’m engaging in the debate on this policy. I seek the support of my colleagues. I seek the support of the public.”
author: Jason Spits
heading: Superannuation and Investments
